# About This Script

This script, as for raw traits, shows the workflow to evaluating the relationship of Community Weighted Mean (CWM) with corrected functional traits and our environmental drivers.
The pipeline executes the following steps:


1) Calculates CWM values for each trait in each phylogenetic scenario.

2) Fits linear models to evaluate relationships between CWM and environmental drivers across scenarios.

3) Tests model residuals for spatial structure using Moran's I and Spatial Eigenvector Maps (MEM) across scenarios.

4) Evaluates model robustness against sampling effort using Cook's distance correlations.


The resulting output of this script is the main content of Table 2 and Appendix S14.

> ![WARNING] 
> Run this script demands a lot of memory (\~4 GB) and take a minute to end. Therefore, clear garbage accumulated with `gc()`, the environment and restart the session. You may not be able to run this script if you have less the 8 GB of RAM memory.

# Packages and setup

```{r}
rm(list = ls()) ## Empty environment
gc()

require(vegan)          # Ecological analysis
library(here)           # Deal with setwd in .qmd archives with RStudio :(, but not in the nvim ;)
library(readxl)         # Read Excel files
library(reshape2)       # Data reshaping
library(SYNCSA)         # SYNCSA for trait-environment modeling
library(openxlsx)       # Exporting Excel
library(tidyverse)      # Data manipulation and visualization
library(foreach)        # Parallel processing (loop)
library(doParallel)     # Parallel backend
library(bbmle)          # AICc model selection
source(here("func/summarize_trees.R"))  # Custom summarizing function 
library(car)


# This function summarizes model selection results across N scenarios.
get_result <- function(sel_md) {
  # For each scenario, extract the best model (delta AICc = 0)
  result_1 <- foreach(i = 1:N) %do%
    {
      cbind.data.frame(
        models = rownames(sel_md[[i]]),
        sel_md[[i]],
        row.names = NULL
      ) %>%
        filter(dAICc == 0)
    } %>%
    plyr::ldply(.fun = data.frame)

  # Summarize the performance of each model across scenarios
  summary <- cbind.data.frame(
    n_sel = tapply(result_1$dAICc, result_1$models, length),          # Times selected as best
    AICc_mean = tapply(result_1$AICc, result_1$models, mean),         # Mean AICc
    AICc_min = round(tapply(result_1$AICc, result_1$models, min), 2), # Min AICc
    AICc_max = round(tapply(result_1$AICc, result_1$models, max), 2), # Max AICc
    dAICc_mean = tapply(result_1$dAICc, result_1$models, mean),       # Mean delta AICc
    dAICc_min = round(tapply(result_1$dAICc, result_1$models, min), 2), # Min delta AICc
    dAICc_max = round(tapply(result_1$dAICc, result_1$models, min), 2), # Max delta AICc
    df = tapply(result_1$df, result_1$models, mean)                   # Degrees of freedom
  )
  return(summary)
}

set.seed(811)          # Ensure reproducibility
options(scipen = 999)  # Disable scientific notation
N = 1000               # Number of iterations (e.g., phylogenetic trees)
```

# Trait Matrix
In this step we will load the organized data, with the original values `org_data` alongside with `S_comp`, i.e., phylogenetic corrected trait for the 1,000 scenarios.

```{r}
S_comp <- readRDS(here("outputs/RDS/SCOMP.RDS"))
org_data <- readRDS(here("data/org_data.RDS"))
```

# Do Parallel Computing

```{r}
no_cores <- detectCores() - 6     # Reserve some CPU cores for system (adjust as needed)
registerDoParallel(cores = no_cores)
cl <- makeCluster(no_cores, type = "FORK")  # Linux/Mac only
```

# Model selection

Now we will select the best model for each trait, as following:
1) Arrange data iteratively with SYNCSA;
2) Creating a list of models names (see Appendix S1 for the hypothesis of each model);
2) Elaborating the linear models, based on the list;
3) Select the most parsimonious models based on AICc;
4) Filter only the best model (dAICc = 0);
5) Save in a new object for summarize in a table.


## Rhizome diameter

```{r}
# Loop over all N iterations for organize data for analysis
or_s_diam <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% {
  organize.syncsa(
    org_data$community,                  # community matrix
    envir = org_data$environmental,      # environmental variables
    traits = data.frame(diam = S_comp$riz_diam[[i]]) # trait: rhizome diameter
  )
}

# Compute community-weighted means (CWM) for rhizome diameter in each dataset
cwm_S_r_diam <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% {
  (matrix.t(
    or_s_diam[[i]]$community,            # community matrix
    or_s_diam[[i]]$traits,               # trait matrix (rhizome diameter)
    scale = F                            # do not scale
  )$matrix.T)                            # extract T matrix (CWM result)
}

# Define candidate linear models (as formulas) to explain rhizome diameter using different predictors
models <- c(
  "Rhiz. Diam ~ MT + plot_size + samp_size",
  "Rhiz. Diam ~ MT + AP + plot_size + samp_size",
  "Rhiz. Diam ~ AP * PS + plot_size + samp_size",
  "Rhiz. Diam ~ N + plot_size + samp_size",
  "Rhiz. Diam ~ CEC + plot_size + samp_size",
  "Rhiz. Diam ~ N + CEC + plot_size + samp_size",
  "Rhiz. Diam ~ PW + plot_size + samp_size",
  "Rhiz. Diam ~ 1" # original model
)


# Fit all candidate models using parallel processing
md1 <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(
    cwm_S_r_diam[[i]] ~ max_temp_wam + plot_size + samp_size,
    data = or_s_diam[[i]]$environmental
  )

md2 <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(
    cwm_S_r_diam[[i]] ~
      max_temp_wam +
        ann_prec +
        plot_size +
        samp_size,
    data = or_s_diam[[i]]$environmental
  )

md3 <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(
    cwm_S_r_diam[[i]] ~
      ann_prec *
        prec_seas +
        plot_size +
        samp_size,
    data = or_s_diam[[i]]$environmental
  )

md4 <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(
    cwm_S_r_diam[[i]] ~ nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size,
    data = or_s_diam[[i]]$environmental
  )

md5 <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(
    cwm_S_r_diam[[i]] ~ cec + plot_size + samp_size,
    data = or_s_diam[[i]]$environmental
  )

md6 <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  lm(
    cwm_S_r_diam[[i]] ~
      nitrogen +
        cec +
        plot_size +
        samp_size,
    data = or_s_diam[[i]]$environmental
  )

md7 <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  glm(
    cwm_S_r_diam[[i]] ~ prec_warm,
    data = or_s_diam[[i]]$environmental
  )


md8 <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar% glm(cwm_S_r_diam[[i]] ~ 1) # original model


sel_md <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    AICctab(
      md1[[i]],
      md2[[i]],
      md3[[i]],
      md4[[i]],
      md5[[i]],
      md6[[i]],
      md7[[i]],
      md8[[i]],
      base = T,
      delta = T,
      mnames = models
    ) %>% `class<-`("data.frame")
    #insert class at ictab
  } %>%
  get_result() # Aggregate results from parallel loop

# View AICc model selection results
sel_diam <- sel_md
sel_diam
# Save the best model for rhizome diameter
model_diam <- md4

```

# Output

The output here is the number that each model was selected as best (dAICc = 0), that is a supplement of Table 2 and Appendix S14.

```{r}
## Elaborate a list of models
a <- list(model_diam,
  model_comp, #compact rhizome
  model_rcr, #short-creeping rhizome
  model_lr, #long-creeping rhizome
  model_mseg, #laminae multipinnate
  model_buds, # proliferous buds
  model_ltri, #trichome in laminae
  model_ind, #indusium and pseudo indusium presence
  model_dim, #laminae dimorphic
  model_spore #spore Chlorophyll
)

# Extract the coefficients from each model 
model_results <- lapply(a, function (x) map_dfr(x, get_model))

head(model_results[[2]])

# Summarize the model coefficients
mod_df <- map_dfr(model_results, function (result){
  result %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      .cols = everything(),
      .fns = function(x) {
        paste0(round(mean(x, na.rm = T),6),"[±", round(sd(x, na.rm=T),6), "]")
      }
      )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(nsel= tapply(result$model, result$model, length), .before = 2)
})

view(mod_df)

#Save data
write.xlsx (x = mod_df, file = here("outputs/summ_models_tcor.xlsx"), rowNames = T)


## Output resumed data
forw <- rbind(
  sel_diam, #rhizome diameter
  sel_rcomp, #compact rhizome
  sel_rcr, #short-creeping rhizomme
  sel_rlr, #long-creeping rhizomme
  sel_lmseg, #laminae multipinnate
  sel_buds, # proliferous buds
  sel_ltri, #trichome in laminae
  sel_ind, #indusium and pseudo indusium presence
  sel_lmorf, #laminae dimorphic
  sel_chl #spore Chlorophyll
) %>%
  mutate(models = rownames(.), .before = n_sel) %>%
  remove_rownames()

## Separate the models without predictors (bad_mods), from the model with at least one
## environmental predictor
rows <- grep("1", forw$models)
nice_mods_Scomp <- forw[-rows, ] # Models w/ env predictors
bad_mods_Scomp <- forw[rows, ] # Models without env. predictor (null models)

## output CWM List
cwm_list <- list()
cwm_list[[1]] <- cwm_S_r_diam
cwm_list[[2]] <- cwm_S_r_comp
cwm_list[[3]] <- cwm_S_r_cr
cwm_list[[4]] <- cwm_S_r_lr
cwm_list[[5]] <- cwm_S_buds
cwm_list[[6]] <- cwm_S_lam_mseg
cwm_list[[7]] <- cwm_S_ltri
cwm_list[[8]] <- cwm_S_chl
cwm_list[[9]] <- cwm_S_lmorf
cwm_list[[10]] <- cwm_S_ind
names(cwm_list) <- c(
  "diam",
  "r_comp",
  "r_cr",
  "r_lr",
  "buds",
  "l_mseg",
  "ltri",
  "chl",
  "lmorf",
  "ind"
)
```

# Robustness of models

To demonstrate model robustness, here we will calculate Cook’s distance of models coefficients. For the phylogenetic corrected models we used the Cook’s distance average for the j-th site as Cj measurement.

The results will be a supplement for Table 2, Appendix S12 and Appendix S14.

```{r}
nice_mods <- list(
  model_diam,
  model_comp, #compact rhizome
  model_rcr, #short-creeping rhizome
  model_mseg, #laminae multipinnate
  model_buds, # proliferous buds
  model_spore #spore Chlorophyll
)
 
# Mesuring cooks distance for models coeficients
cook <- sapply(nice_mods, function (x) {
  sapply(x, cooks.distance) %>%
    rowMeans(.) # We will extract the mean for j-th site to be concise
})

# Add trait names in the cooks distance matrix
colnames(cook) <- c("diam",
                    "r_comp",
                    "r_cr",
                    "l_mseg",
                    "buds",
                    "chl")

# Transforming in df and adding sample size
cook_d <-
  cbind.data.frame(samp_size = org_data$environmental$samp_size
                   [match(rownames(org_data$environmental),# Names must match 
                          rownames(cook))], cook) 

# Save data 
# saveRDS(cook_d, file = "outputs/cook_tcor.RDS")

# Loading again if needed
# cook_d <- readRDS(here("outputs/cook_tcor.RDS"))

shapiro.test(cook_d$samp_size)

# Computing kendall correlation of cook's distance and sample size
kendall_results <- sapply(2:7, USE.NAMES = TRUE, function(x) {
  y <- cook_d[, x]
  samp <- cook_d$samp_size
  test <- cor.test(y, samp, method = "kendall")
  data <- c(tau = as.numeric(test$estimate),
            p_value = as.numeric(test$p.value))
  data
})

# Adding colnames in the resulting matrix
colnames(kendall_results) <- colnames(cook_d)[-1]

# Transforming in a transpose df 
kendall_summary <- as.data.frame(t(round(kendall_results,2)))
write.xlsx(kendall_summary, here("outputs/CS_tcor.xlsx"))

# Creating a vector with real names of traits to use in the final plots
names <- c(
  "Rhiz. Diameter",
  "Rhiz. Compact",
  "Rhiz. Short-Creeping",
  "Lam. Multipinnate",
  "Buds presence",
  "Spore Chlorophyll"
)


# Plotting data for visual inspection
tiff(
  file = here("figs/cook_tcor.tiff"),
  width = 180,
  height = 100,
  units = "mm",
  res = 300)

par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

sapply(1:6, function(i) {
  cook <- cook_d[, -1]
  col_name <- cook[, i]
  name <- names[i]
  plot(
    y = col_name,
    x = log10(cook_d$samp_size),
    cex.main = 0.8,
    ylab = "Cook's Distance",
    xlab = "Sample effort (log10)",
    main = paste0(name, " (Cor.)"),
    pch = 15,
    col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.5),
    ylim = c(0, 2)
  )
  abline(h = 1, col = "red", lty = 2) # abline in D = 1 limit common limit for really influential points
})

dev.off()


```
